$comment: THE TWIN REGISTER — every capability whose logic has been COLLAPSED into an
@ai-matrx/* package. A local definition of one of these names in this repo is a
re-grown twin: the exact failure the client-package campaign exists to kill
(Arman: 'the logic of the packages is NEVER duplicated outside of the package').
Add a row the same session you delete a twin. Never add an allowlist entry to
silence a NEW twin — an allowlist entry is only for a definition that is
PROVABLY not the same capability, and it must say why in `reason`.

A WRAPPER is not a twin: a local function that BINDS the package function's options (unit, style, fallback) and delegates in a line or two is the sanctioned adapter, and needs no entry. A re-implemented BODY is a twin, always.

A SHAPE rule (`shapeWhy` + `shapeAllow` + `shapeCensus` on a row) catches the same capability under an UNREGISTERED name, or with no name at all. `shapeAllow` = provably NOT this capability, silent. `shapeCensus` = pre-existing bodies that ARE it and are not collapsed yet: loud every run, shrink-only, and a stale entry fails the guard.

twins.name: formatUsd
twins.why: THE honest money formatter (kit 0.12.0, 2026-09-12). `$${(cost ?? 0).toFixed(4)}` rendered "$0.0000" for a cost NOBODY MEASURED and a reader walked away believing the run was free; the same `?? 0` then went into a SUM, so an unmeasured cost was invisible inside an analytics total that rode into an agent payload. Unknown is an em-dash, a MEASURED zero is still "$0.00". Named Usd not Currency under the UNIT LAW: it prepends a literal `$` with no locale handling, and a EUR amount wearing a `$` is the same class of lie. Census: currency in ~85 files across four clients with zero package coverage before this.
twins.shapeWhy: A number becoming a MONEY string is this capability whatever it is called. The NAME lane read formatUsd as adopted and clean while matrx-frontend's features/admin/spend/format.ts exported `usd` and `usdPrecise` bodies that NINE live Spend Dashboard and Spend Explorer components import, UsageTableClient.tsx exported `fmtCost` with ten call sites, features/hindsight/components/tokens.ts exported a third `fmtCost` IN A FILE THAT ALREADY IMPORTS KIT, and 22 more files built an Intl.NumberFormat with style:"currency" by hand. The bodies did not merely duplicate the package, they disagreed with it and with their own comments: `usdPrecise(0.000004)` returned "$0.0000" under a doc comment promising sub-cent visibility, and `fmtCost` rendered a $0.004 total_cost as "$0.00" in the VIEWER's locale, so a German admin read "0,00 $". Pattern and its proof: scripts/money-shape.mjs. A `$` in a regex or a shell string can never match — money is EXACTLY two dollars (one is the interpolation marker, three is LaTeX display math), a Postgres positional parameter interpolates a loop index and is excluded by name, and `/ 100` as a percentage step is excluded because the cents arm requires the dividend to NAME itself cents or millicents. `shapeCensus` below is the pre-existing census, not an exemption: it is reported every run and is ratcheted shrink-only — a stale entry FAILS the guard.

twins.name: formatPercentFromFraction
twins.why: The percentage half of the honest-number contract (~149 files, zero package coverage before kit 0.12.0). The long name is the point: half the fleet's twins took a 0..1 fraction and half took a 0..100 percentage, a 100x error that renders plausibly, so the unit is in the name. twins.name: safeRatio
twins.why: The indeterminate-division guard behind formatPercentFromFraction. `0 / 0` is not zero, it is unknown, and this returns null for it rather than letting NaN reach the screen as "NaN% used".

twins.name: sumKnown
twins.why: THE function that closes the lying-screen class. `?? 0` was never typed in front of a formatter — it was typed in front of `+`, because a nullable number must become a number before it can be added. This returns { total, known, unknown } so a caller cannot present a total as complete without ignoring a field it was handed, and it is the only thing that separates "all zero" from "nothing measured".

twins.name: isKnownNumber

twins.name: formatRelativeTime
twins.why: THE relative-timestamp formatter, unified 2026-09-07 from @ai-matrx/associations (the Intl voice) and @ai-matrx/diff (the dense '2m ago' voice) plus twelve matrx-frontend copies. Three styles behind one body: short / long / intl, plus fallback and fallbackToInput.

Pattern and its proof: scripts/relative-time-shape.mjs. An age used only to pick a BRANCH formats nothing and can never match; a WINDOW between two given stamps is a duration, so only Date.now() and a no-argument new Date() count as the clock; a ticking countdown ("in 30s") is formatDurationMs's and the future prefix is deliberately not a voice; and a function that does ANY time-base division is never reported by arm B, so one body can never open in two register rows.

twins.name: formatFileSize
twins.why: THE byte-size formatter. It was hiding inside @ai-matrx/media's UploadProgressList React component, so six matrx-frontend twins could only reach it by depending on the media React bundle to print a byte count. Moved to kit 2026-09-07 with the display decisions written down (binary units, short labels, one decimal below ten in a unit, whole bytes below 1 KB, em-dash for unknown/negative — NEVER a confident '0 B'). 2026-09-11: the name lane read GREEN while 134 byte-size bodies lived in 67 files under OTHER names — this row now also carries the SHAPE rule below, which is what actually closed the class.
twins.shapeWhy: A byte count becoming a unit string is this capability whatever it is called. The 2026-09-07 census predicted this gap ('the census method needs a shape pass') and the 2026-09-11 re-verification proved it: formatBytes, fmtBytes, humanSize, bytesHuman, formatSize, and ~60 bare inline JSX expressions that are not definitions at all and can never be caught by a name. A second review the same day proved the rule was blind to the DECIMAL (SI) family — 1000 / 1e6 / 1_000_000 — and to a GB-input body that MULTIPLIES; five live twins were returning zero findings. Both are covered now. Pattern and its proof: scripts/byte-size-shape.mjs. A capacity constant can never match: the division arms require a DIVISION or THRESHOLD COMPARISON against a byte base, and the multiply arm requires BOTH a non-literal operand (so 80 * 1024 * 1024 is out) AND the unit label on the same line outside any comment (so `limitMb * 1024 * 1024; // 25 MB` is out). This repo has ~60 legitimate byte ceilings that must stay untouched.

twins.name: createBrowserClient
twins.why: The BROWSER Supabase client. Hand-rolling it re-grows the whole hazard set @ai-matrx/data/next owns: the auth-cookie options (a client on the default cookie name cannot see the session the other doors wrote), the globalThis-slot singleton (a per-module one splits auth state across ESM and CJS graphs), and static NEXT_PUBLIC_* member access (a dynamic lookup is undefined in every browser bundle). matrx-games' utils/supabase/client.ts body was deleted 2026-09-07 in favour of supabaseNext.browserClient(). Import the name from @supabase/ssr only inside the package.

twins.name: createServerClient
twins.why: The SSR Supabase client and, with it, the cookie getAll/setAll dance that had been copied into three files here (server, middleware, and the AI Matrx OAuth callback route). The package owns serverClient / routeClient / middlewareSession: the swallowed Server-Component cookie write, the legacy storage-key migration, the split-jar heal, the 'nothing may run between construction and getUser()' rule, no-store headers and cookie carry-over onto redirects. Every one of those has logged users out at random at least once. All four matrx-games sites were collapsed 2026-09-07.

twins.name: base64ByteLength
twins.why: THE decoded byte length of base64 text (kit 0.13.5, 2026-09-12). There is exactly ONE honest way to compute it and five live sites had written it five ways: `b64.length * 3 / 4` OVERSTATES every padded payload by one or two bytes, because four base64 characters carry three bytes and a trailing `=` / `==` is exactly the bytes that were never there. A sixth adversarial review fixed three sites by hand; a seventh found a FOURTH still wrong (matrx-extend tools/handlers/read.ts, feeding size_bytes) and two of the repairs living as private copies under this same name in aidream's dashboard and in matrx-local. A capability re-derived from memory at every call site is a package export nobody had written yet. The number it returns is real BYTES, which is what formatFileSize wants — the input lane exists because a base64 STRING LENGTH reaching that formatter prints a confident, wrong " KB". NOTE 2026-09-12: the module landed in this repo for kit 0.13.5 but is NOT in the published 0.13.5 tarball — that release was cut from a tree that predated it. The two npm consumers (matrx-extend, matrx-local) therefore still carry censused local copies, and they are blocked on a kit release that actually contains the module, not on a version number.
